Akmene Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Šiaulių apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Jews first settled in Akmenė in the mid-18th century, making up around two-thirds of the town's population in the first half of the 19th; many were later expelled to central Russia during WWI and never returned. At the end of June 1941, following the German invasion, Akmenė's Jews were transferred to barracks near Mažeikiai and murdered on August 9, 1941, together with the Jews of Mažeikiai and its surroundings. This cemetery, likely opened in the second half of the 18th century, alongside the town's founding Jewish community, holds tombstones ranging from 1866 to 1925, most inscribed in Hebrew, some in Yiddish; it was registered in Lithuania's Register of Immovable Cultural Property in 2003.
